sections.overview: Leucocarbo carunculatus, the kawau pāteketeke or New Zealand king shag, is an endemic seabird of New Zealand.
sections.identification: This large shag is black and white with pink feet; breeding adults develop yellow fleshy caruncles at the base of the bill.
sections.habitat: It is confined to the outer Marlborough Sounds, nesting on rocky islets and foraging in nearby coastal waters, mostly less than 50 metres deep.
sections.behavior: These sensitive birds travel from their colonies to offshore feeding grounds and can be disturbed by boats near nesting and roosting sites.
sections.reproduction: Most breeding occurs in winter; nests are platforms of sticks and seaweed on rock faces or plateaus, and clutches usually contain 1–3 pale-blue eggs.
sections.ecology: Pied shags are similar in size; the related Stewart Island shag has a slimmer bill and orange rather than yellow breeding caruncles.
sections.conservation: It is classified as Nationally Endangered in New Zealand; its restricted range leaves the population vulnerable to severe weather, disturbance, fishing nets and changes to coastal food webs.
